We also introduce MUSES, a multi-source ensemble of secondary structures designed to mitigate predictor bias, and a dynamic masking ratio that balances structure-guided and nucleotide-level masking. structRFM learns joint sequence and structure representations as sequence-level, nucleotide-level and pairwise features for broad downstream adaptation. It ranks among the leading models in zero-shot homology classification and establishes new benchmarks for secondary-structure prediction. Its tertiary-structure adaptation, Zfold, consistently improves both three-dimensional predictions and their extracted secondary structures, with performance comparable to AlphaFold3 across CASP15-natural, CASP16 and RNA-Puzzles. structRFM also improves performance on function-prediction tasks and generalizes to newly released RNA families and long non-coding RNAs. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of structure-guided pre-training and highlight multimodal RNA language models for robust structural and functional inference. The complete 21-million-pair dataset, model weights and source code are openly available to support multimodal RNA foundation-model development.

items.title: Longitudinal AI Models Predict Cancer Adverse Events
items.abstract_or_text: Clinical interventions for cancer treatment toxicities can reduce morbidity, mortality, and healthcare cost, if high risk patients can be identified. We developed SPARC, a transformer-based foundation model, using real-world, longitudinal, routinely collected health measurements, to predict adverse event risk. Pre-training and fine-tuning SPARC on 101,920,379 measurements from 224,047 patients with cancer led to state-of-the-art performance at predicting cancer-related adverse events on (i) held-out data from the development cohort, (ii) a prospective validation cohort from the same center (Npatients=23,126), (iii) multiple publicly available external datasets (Npatients=26,012), and (iv) external, multi-hospital cohorts (Npatients=562,620, 206,840). SPARC generalized to multiple external centers and identified patients most likely to benefit from an intervention (G-CSF). Pooled multi-institution, more than single-institution, fine-tuning improved generalizability. We release SPARC as a community resource. Our results highlight the utility of AI time series models in oncologic management.

items.title: DiaBench: A Benchmarking Framework to Evaluate the Performance of LLMs in T2D Patient Education
items.abstract_or_text: Background Effective type 2 diabetes (T2D) education improves patient outcomes, but clinician time constraints limit what can be covered during encounters. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable way to answer patient questions, yet their accuracy and reliability in T2D education across health literacy levels remain poorly characterized. Methods We developed DiaBench, a standardized benchmarking framework built from 96 question-and-answer pairs collected by clinicians from representative real-world patient encounters. GPT-5 transformed each pair into multiple-choice questions (MCQs) under three configurations (1-3) simulating different question formats and levels of user background. A five-member panel of certified diabetes care and education specialists (CDCESs), medical doctors (MDs), and endocrinologists validated the transformations, rating question rephrasing, answer rephrasing, and answer correctness. We then evaluated seven LLMs (GPT-51, Gemini-2.5-Flash2, Cohere Command3, Llama-44, DeepSeek-R15, Perplexity Sonar6, Mistral-Large-2.07) for accuracy and self-consistency across three runs. Results (i) Expert validation showed a consensus over MCQ transformation. For configuration 1, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of rephrased answers were appropriate, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of MCQ answers were correct, and 95.0% (SD 0.05) of rephrased questions were appropriate; corresponding values for configuration 2 were 96.3% (SD 0.05), 97.5% (SD 0.02), and 89.8% (SD 0.14). (ii) across benchmarking for configurations 1 and 2, most models achieved high accuracy ([≥]95%), but Mistral-Large-2.0, Llama 4, and Perplexity Sonar showed substantially lower self-consistency (60.4%-91.7%) than other models ([≥]95%). All models degraded in both accuracy and self-consistency on configuration 3. Conclusions DiaBench quantitatively differentiates LLM capability in T2D patient education, with Gemini, GPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 performing strongly and other models suboptimally. DiaBench provides a transferable platform for evaluating existing and newly developed LLMs, addressing the need for standardized benchmarking before clinical deployment of LLM-based systems in patient education.

items.title: LLMs as Judges and Examinees for Medical Item Difficulty Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Predicting medical item difficulty from item text alone remains challenging. Prior work has largely relied on linguistic features or text representations derived from general-purpose and domain-specific language models, but predictive performance has remained modest. This study takes a different approach by using difficulty-related signals that emerge when open-weight large language models (LLMs) interact with test items. Using USMLE and PANCE medical licensure examination items, we examined LLMs in two roles. As judges, the models provided absolute difficulty ratings and pairwise difficulty comparisons. As simulated examinees, they generated response-based signals including correctness, keyed-option probability, response entropy, and the probability margin between the top two options. We then combined the strongest judgment and response signals with baseline item features in downstream prediction models. Pairwise difficulty judgment was the most consistent individual LLM signal across both datasets, while simulated-examinee signals and absolute judgments provided complementary information in some feature combinations. The best configurations reached a Spearman correlation of ρ = .447 on USMLE, exceeding the best system in the 2024 BEA shared task (ρ = .25), and ρ = .494 on PANCE. These results were comparable to direct absolute judgments from the proprietary frontier model Claude Opus 5 (ρ = .443 and .488, respectively). Overall, judgment and response signals from open-weight LLMs captured difficulty-related information beyond text representations. Because these models can be deployed locally, the approach offers a practical option for predicting the difficulty of unreleased or high-security test items.

items.title: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
items.abstract_or_text: Clinical large language models are increasingly fielded as multi-agent teams, on the assumption that deliberation averages out individual error. It does not average out bias. Across a full factorial of five model families and four aggregation topologies on 120 real MIMIC-IV emergency cases under counterfactual demographic swaps, no configuration neutralizes the disparity: all 20 cells commit the direction of their agents' independent answers, giving Black patients more acute triage. Every model has a topology that amplifies its baseline gap, but which one varies by model, so no design is reliably safe or reliably amplifying: the disparity is relocated, never removed. Late-stage fixes fail: fairness instructions and demographic masking leave the gap untouched, and per-agent self-debiasing widens it, because the bias is already encoded in the agents' ordinary clinical numbers. We call this disparity laundering; the audits now applied to clinical AI, per model, per output, per version, can certify the parts but never the committed decision. Interventions close the gap exactly when they make counterfactual versions visible inside the system and pool them, through deliberation, into the committed decision. A diverse-perspective ensemble does both while keeping the team, with no retraining or architectural change: the disparity falls by 67 to 94% where all five perspectives pool at every round, and the one topology that never pools them is the one it cannot reliably repair. Medical multi-agent systems do not filter demographic bias; they launder it into plausible decisions no single-version audit can catch, and the only defense is to make the bias visible.

items.title: Deep Learning Based Cell Segmentation of 3D Confocal Images of Wood for Enzymatic Hydrolysis Applications
items.abstract_or_text: Plant cell walls are an abundant renewable resource for biobased products, but their recalcitrance limits enzymatic hydrolysis efficiency. Cell and tissue morphological parameters provide reliable biomarkers for predicting enzymatic hydrolysis efficiency. Accurate cell segmentation in 3D microscopy images is essential for quantifying these parameters. Although deep learning has achieved high performance in biological image segmentation, confocal microscopy's limited penetration depth leaves elongated wood cells partially imaged, creating open-ended structures that challenge existing segmentation methods. Based on an artificial longitudinal domain restriction, an adapted framework is presented here for the training of a 3D U-net model for the cell segmentation of wood images. Quantitative evaluation on a dedicated benchmark dataset identified a model configuration that reduced segmentation errors and produced more robust predictions during early enzymatic hydrolysis. These results support the use of the framework to quantify morphological parameters relevant to assessing and predicting biomass conversion efficiency.

items.title: MultiFlow: coupled flow matching for predicting single-cell multiomic perturbation responses in unseen cellular contexts
items.abstract_or_text: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation requires resolving coordinated changes across molecular layers, yet most single-cell perturbation models focus on transcriptional responses alone. Here we present MultiFlow, a coupled flow-matching framework that unifies generation and perturbation prediction of paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Through bidirectional information exchange between RNA and ATAC generative flows, MultiFlow learns how their joint distribution depends on cellular context and perturbation identity. Across multiomic generation benchmarks, MultiFlow accurately reproduced paired RNA-ATAC states and their population distributions. In multiome perturbation benchmarks, MultiFlow achieved the strongest overall performance in predicting both gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility perturbation responses, outperforming modality-specific perturbation-prediction methods in cell types whose perturbed states were withheld from training. Joint multiomic modeling further preserved perturbation-induced coordination between modalities, including concordant peak-gene effects and cross-modal cellular neighborhood structure. These results establish MultiFlow as a unified generative framework for modeling paired molecular states and predicting their coordinated perturbation responses across cellular contexts. Code and tutorial of MultiFlow are available at https://github.com/liuq-lab/MultiFlow.

items.title: Antibody Fragment-Based TROP-2 Targeting: Preclinical Evaluation of of ¹⁷⁷Lu-Sacituzumab F(ab’)₂ for Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP-2) is highly expressed in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and several other solid tumors, making it an attractive target for radiotheranostic applications. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a 177 Lu-labeled F(ab')₂ fragment of Sacituzumab as a TROP-2–targeted radiotheranostic agent.F(ab')₂ fragments of Sacituzumab were generated by pepsin digestion and conjugated with p-SCN-Bn-CHX-A″-DTPA, followed by radiolabeling with 177 Lu. The resulting radioconjugate was characterized using chromatographic techniques. In vitro cell-binding and saturation-binding studies were performed in several cell lines to assess specificity and binding affinity. In vivo biodistribution studies were conducted in T47D- and SK-OV-3 tumor-bearing nude mouse models. Results F(ab')₂-Sacituzumab fragments were obtained with an approximate yield of 55% and were successfully conjugated with CHX-A″-DTPA. Radiolabeling with 177 Lu achieved a radiochemical purity of > 98% after purification. In vitro studies demonstrated specific uptake in T47D, MDA-MB-231, and SK-OV-3 cells, while saturation-binding assays confirmed high-affinity binding to TROP-2–expressing cells. Biodistribution studies showed substantial tumor accumulation in both tumor xenografts, with predominant renal clearance and minimal uptake in non-target tissues. High tumor-to-background ratios were observed, indicating favorable pharmacokinetic behavior. Conclusions [ 177 Lu]Lu-DTPA-F(ab')₂-Sacituzumab demonstrated strong and selective targeting of TROP-2–expressing tumors, favorable biodistribution, and efficient tumor localization. These findings support its potential as a promising radiotheranostic agent for TNBC and other TROP-2–overexpressing malignancies and warrant further translational and clinical evaluation.

items.title: Generative-AI Rewriting and the Robustness of Health Misinformation Detection: A Cross-Dataset Evaluation of Failure Mechanisms and Mitigation
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background: Generative AI can alter the surface form, fluency, rhetorical organisation, and evidential register of a health claim without necessarily changing its underlying proposition. High original-text accuracy therefore does not establish model robustness to claim-preserving rewriting, introducing a critical vulnerability into automated public health infrastructure and personalised digital health tools. Objective: To quantify how ChatGPT-based neutral, ELM central-route, and ELM peripheral-route transformations alter health-misinformation detector performance, computational persuasion features, and detector failure mechanisms, and to evaluate whether transformation-aware training mitigates detector failures and improves the reliability of automated health-information assessment. Methods: COVID-19 FNIR and Monkeypox corpora were evaluated under a paired C0–C3 design using four classical and five CNN/recurrent detectors. A balanced 200-root intervention cohort was generated with one C1–C3 descendant per condition. For mitigation, each dataset's intervention roots were divided into 50 augmentation roots and 50 untouched mitigation-test roots; C0-only augmentation was compared with C0+C1–C3 transformation-aware augmentation. Results: Across the initial intervention panel, macro-F1 fell from 0.987 to 0.428–0.479 on FNIR and from 0.922 to 0.731–0.781 on Monkeypox. Failure modes differed sharply, revealing distinct information-quality risks relevant to digital health safeguards. FNIR failure was dominated by false-positive inflation, indicating a risk of incorrectly flagging reliable health information, whereas mpox showed substantial increases in misinformation false negatives, indicating a risk of failing to identify rewritten misleading claims. Transformation-aware training increased mean C1–C3 macro-F1 on unseen Monkeypox roots by 0.148 across nine models (9/9 improved; Wilcoxon p=0.0039) while preserving panel-level C0 performance (+0.004). FNIR mitigation was smaller and heterogeneous (+0.035; 7/9 models improved; p=0.164), and cross-dataset transfer was inconsistent. Conclusions: Generative-AI rewriting produced substantial, dataset-dependent deterioration in health-misinformation detector performance, even under transformation instructions intended to preserve the underlying claims. Transformation-aware augmentation improved in-domain robustness, particularly for mpox, but did not consistently generalise across datasets. These findings support the inclusion of transformation-based stress testing and class-specific error analysis when evaluating potential automated health-information safeguards. Independent semantic-fidelity validation and application-specific evaluation remain necessary before clinical deployment implications can be established.

items.title: Parameters for stable Notch-independent Her6 oscillations across a frequency spectrum in neural stem cell populations
items.abstract_or_text: Neural proliferation zones drive strong and persistent growth of the developing vertebrate brain. How Notch signaling and HES/Her transcription factors in vivo maintain stable neural stem cell (NSC) populations during brain growth is not well understood. Genetic evidence revealed Her6, a Notch-independent homolog of mammalian HES1, to be essential for maintenance of zebrafish NSCs. We recombined mNeonGreen into the her6 locus and analyzed temporal Her6-mNG fluorescence profiles in vivo. Her6 is expressed dynamically in all NSCs, with a majority revealing stable oscillation, albeit from cell to cell across a wide frequency range. Her6 oscillates cell-autonomously, unaffected by inhibition of Notch, and is robustly reinitiated after experimental perturbations. Mathematical modelling predicts, and we indeed find in vivo, that Her6 oscillations prevail only when both transcript and protein degradation rate constants are equal. These intrinsic control parameters may have evolved for the Her6 oscillator to contribute to robust maintenance of NSCs.

items.title: Advancing Clinical Genomic Analysis with a Skill-Centred Agent
items.abstract_or_text: Clinical genomic analysis requires experts to integrate evolving guidelines, databases, and computational evidence. As sequencing has become increasingly accessible, this complex and labor-intensive process has become a major bottleneck to the timely use of genomic information in clinical decision-making. To fill this gap, we developed ClinGeX, a large-language-model agent that composes 105 curated executable skills through task-specific retrieval and dependency-aware orchestration. On 223 temporally held-out benchmark cases, ClinGeX achieved 71.7\% macro-averaged task-level concordance with expert reference classifications, compared with 45.7\% for the strongest comparator. In a three-condition, counterbalanced human-AI collaboration study, 45 clinical genomic professionals assessed 135 clinically derived cases under routine (no AI assistance), DeepSeek-assisted and ClinGeX-assisted conditions. ClinGeX assistance increased raw case-level concordance across criterion-level variant analysis, genomic interpretation in rare disease and molecular oncology decision-making (51.1\%, 57.8\%, 64.4\% versus 15.6\%, 31.1\%, 20.0\% in comparator conditions) and reduced reported interpretation time in all scenarios. During an exploratory one-month real-world non-interventional assessment, 11 experienced professionals submitted feedback on 96 self-selected analysis episodes and reported frequent conclusion adoption and time savings. These findings support executable domain skills as a promising approach to augment specialist genomic interpretation.

items.title: The Athlete as a Scientist of One: Agentic Bayesian Experimental Design for Individualized Physiology from Consumer Wearables
items.abstract_or_text: Large language model (LLM) agents for personal health read wearable data and recommend, but do not learn about the individual in a way that can be audited or falsified. We present EpiCoach, an agentic system that treats one athlete, a cross-country mountain biker, as the subject of accountable N-of-1 science. Claims about the athlete live in an evidence-gated hypothesis registry: each must issue a probabilistic prediction about a future session before it occurs, and its belief moves only through computed evidence from a logged statistical fit. Predictions come from a mechanistic digital twin inferred from heart rate, GPS and barometric altitude: a lagged heart-rate response model, a fitness-fatigue model with learned time constants, and a latent technical-descending skill state, measured on discovered trail segments. The agent prescribes the next training week as a constrained experiment maximizing information gain subject to load and safety constraints, around two instrument rides. We evaluate the system two ways over eighteen months of data. A rolling-origin replay benchmark shows the twin beats standard forecasters on heart rate but not segment time, and the agentic loop matches a static model. A live prospective phase runs the weekly cycle: in its first three weeks the ledger sealed 20 predictions, scored 14, the descent forecast calibrated after one correction, the climb forecast pessimistic as the athlete improved, and the safety officer vetoed the agent twice. Every correction is preserved in the registry, a template for auditable, falsifiable personalization in digital health. We release the registry, benchmark and protocol.

items.title: What Makes Medical Examination Items Difficult? Using Large Language Models to Explore Patterns Associated With Empirical Item Difficulty
items.abstract_or_text: Research on medical item difficulty has largely focused on prediction rather than on identifying interpretable patterns associated with empirical difficulty. This study used empirical difficulty labels to guide large language models (LLMs) in inducing difficulty rubrics and examined how rubric guidance affected LLM difficulty judgments. Using training items and their empirical difficulty estimates from the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) and the Physician Assistant National Certifying Examination (PANCE), Claude Opus 5 induced separate rubrics for absolute and pairwise difficulty judgment. None of the induced rubrics treated surface features, such as stem length, option count, or images, as major sources of difficulty. Several patterns emerged across both examinations, including cue convergence, misleading cues, and option competition, although their specific forms differed. Retrieval of knowledge that could not be derived from the stem was particularly prominent in the PANCE rubrics, whereas the USMLE rubrics placed greater emphasis on integrating multiple clinical cues. We compared commercial and open-weight LLMs on held-out items under unguided and rubric-guided conditions. Rubric guidance changed how models used the difficulty scale but did not consistently improve performance. In absolute judgments, guidance encouraged broader use of the scale and generally improved coarse-grained agreement, without consistently improving rank ordering. In pairwise comparisons, its effects varied across models and examinations, and judgments became more sensitive to presentation order. These findings suggest that the value of label-guided rubric induction may lie more in generating interpretable, testable hypotheses from empirical difficulty data than in reliably improving difficulty judgments.

items.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
items.abstract_or_text: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. Here, we analyzed a pan-pediatric scRNA-seq atlas of 266 patient- and xenograft-derived samples across 22 pediatric solid tumor types. To address the bottleneck between gene program identification and interpretation, we developed an AI agent framework built on off-the-shelf large language models (e.g., Gemini 2.5) to interpret gene expression programs at the level of human experts, but at much greater scale and speed. Our agent identified ectopic expression of neuronal marker genes as a unique feature of several fusion-driven sarcomas. This gene expression pattern resulted in tumor-specific co-expression of mixed mesenchymal/neuronal surface markers, providing a plausible therapeutic window to target these tumor types using emerging AND-gated therapeutic strategies, such as bispecific antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and bispecific CAR-T cells. As proof of principle, we nominated and validated STEAP1/NPTXR as a Ewing sarcoma candidate cell surface target pair. Together, this work delivers a pan-pediatric solid tumor scRNA-seq atlas, establishes a generalizable and accessible AI-based framework that complements existing single-cell methods by automating interpretation of pan-disease single-cell atlases, and nominates new bispecific ADC/CAR-T targets for catastrophic pediatric cancers.

items.title: Bacterial Species Classification from Full-Plate Culture Images Using Deep Learning: A Comparative Study of CNNs and Vision Transformers
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Accurate identification of bacterial species from culture plates is essential for microbiological analysis, yet conventional identification procedures can be time-consuming and dependent on specialized expertise. This study investigates the feasibility of automated multiclass bacterial identification directly from complete culture-plate images and compares convolutional and transformer-based deep-learning architectures under a unified experimental protocol. A balanced dataset comprising 950 high-resolution images representing 19 clinically relevant bacterial species was used. ResNet50, DenseNet121, and ViT-B/16 were fine-tuned using identical input resolution, training-only data augmentation, optimization settings, and stratified five-fold cross-validation. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, macro-precision, macro-recall, macro F1-score, Matthews correlation coefficient, Cohen’s kappa, class-wise performance, and aggregated out-of-fold error analysis. ViT-B/16 achieved the best overall performance, with a mean accuracy of 99.05 ± 0.86% and macro F1-score of 99.05 ± 0.86%, followed by DenseNet121 with 97.58 ± 1.69% accuracy and ResNet50 with 94.21 ± 1.75%. ViT-B/16 also achieved MCC and Cohen’s kappa values of approximately 0.99 and produced only nine misclassifications across the aggregated out-of-fold predictions. Class-wise analysis showed consistently high performance across most bacterial species, with errors concentrated in a limited number of visually challenging class pairs. These findings demonstrate the potential of deep-learning models, particularly Vision Transformers, for accurate whole-plate bacterial species classification without prior extraction of individual colonies. The study provides a reproducible comparative baseline for CNN- and transformer-based bacterial image classification and motivates future strain-independent and multi-centre validation.

items.title: The Dual-Use Nature of Large Language Models in Cybersecurity: A Bibliometric Analysis and Critical Review
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) now occupy three positions in cybersecurity at once: they are systems that must be secured, capabilities that lower the cost of offence, and instruments that augment defence. Existing reviews typically examine one of these roles in isolation, which obscures how the roles interact and leaves the field without an evidence base for judging whether the interactions are being studied. This article addresses that gap by combining a VOSviewer-based bibliometric analysis with a critical literature review. We retrieved 13,756 records published between January 2023 and 19 October 2026 from OpenAlex and, after document-type, language, abstract, de-duplication and validated relevance screening (precision 84.0%, 95% CI 78.3–88.4%), analysed 7,369 documents through performance analysis, keyword co-occurrence and co-citation mapping in VOSviewer and a dictionary-based classification of each document's dual-use role. The co-occurrence map resolves into four thematic clusters: attacks on and alignment of LLMs; LLM-enabled detection and security operations; code and vulnerability analysis, including penetration testing; and socio-technical threats and governance. Research on LLMs as targets (42.8% of documents) and as defensive tools (35.3%) has grown largely in parallel: only 7.9% of documents address more than one role, and only 11.1% of defensive studies engage with attacks on the defending model itself, falling to 2.5% for vulnerability detection. The critical review explains why this matters: reported success rates of offensive LLM agents range from 0% to 90% depending on experimental design, few defences are evaluated against adaptive adversaries, and the security–utility trade-off is rarely quantified. We formalise these findings in a coupled dual-use framework with three testable propositions and derive eight research directions, prioritising adaptive evaluation, multilingual guardrail robustness, longitudinal measurement and the security of defensive LLM deployments.

items.title: From enrollment to sequencing: cancer microbiome methods reporting is inconsistent and incomplete
items.abstract_or_text: Reproducibility in microbiome research depends on transparent reporting of sample sizes and sequence counts both before and after quality control (QC) processes. This is an expectation formalized in the STORMS (Strengthening The Organization and Reporting of Microbiome Studies) checklist published in November 2021. Whether cancer microbiome studies comply with the STORMS items governing sample size, sequencing and quality control, however, remains largely unexamined. Here, we audited 67 clinical cancer microbiome studies against ten STORMS items that apply to every microbiome study, spanning participant and sample counts, laboratory processing, sequencing, bioinformatic processing and experimental controls. Nearly all studies reported their number of participants (96%) and final number of samples analyzed (97%). However, STORMS items beyond sample sizes were largely underreported, ranging from 9% to 36%. The median study reported two of these eight methods items, and 16 studies reported none. Reporting did not change measurably after STORMS was published and was unrelated to journal impact factor. Because aspects like read normalization, quality-control filtering, taxa removal, and contamination handling directly affect the end result of a cancer microbiome study, differences in how these are implemented can have critical implications for the field’s reproducibility as well as rigor at large. Resolving this issue will require buy-in from scientists, funding institutions, and journals to work together to enforce stricter standards for cancer microbiome methodology reporting.

items.title: Keepace.ai: A Technical Report on a Large Language Model for Sports and Health
items.abstract_or_text: Large language models hold promise for delivering safe, scientifically grounded, and personalized exercise guidance at scale, yet the sports-and-health domain still lacks curated training corpora and rigorous evaluation benchmarks. Keepace.ai is a domain-specialized LLM built on Qwen3.5-27B through post-training, currently optimized for Chinese-language exercise guidance across three tasks: workout plan generation, sports-and-health knowledge QA, and personal sports data analysis. In internal rubric-based evaluations designed with domain experts, Keepace.ai outperforms its base model and larger general-purpose baselines, with the most pronounced improvements in exercise safety, boundary compliance, structured output completeness, and scientific accuracy. This report summarizes the current design, data pipeline, safety-first evaluation framework, and evaluation results of Keepace.ai.

items.title: VIPER-seq: Protein-mediated small RNA enrichment enhances plant virus detection at low viral abundance
items.abstract_or_text: Early and accurate detection of viral infections is critical for effective disease management and biosecurity programs. High-throughput sequencing technologies have emerged as powerful tools for plant disease diagnostics. In particular, sequencing of virus-derived small RNAs (vsiRNAs) enables the simultaneous detection of both known and novel viral agents. Compared with other approaches, small RNA sequencing (sRNA-seq) can offer superior sensitivity because it is less affected by the abundance of host messenger and ribosomal RNAs (mRNA and rRNA, respectively), and because sRNAs are generally more stable than longer RNA molecules. However, the sensitivity of sRNA-seq can be compromised by the presence of abundant endogenous small RNAs, which dilute the viral signal and hinder pathogen detection, particularly in low-titre infections. Here, we present VIPER-seq (Viral small RNA Isolation by Protein-mediated Enrichment and Recovery sequencing), a method that exploits sRNA-binding proteins to enrich vsiRNAs prior to high-throughput sequencing. Using cucumber seeds infected with cucumber green mottle mosaic virus (CGMMV), we demonstrate that VIPER-seq substantially enhances the detection of infected plant material compared with conventional sRNA-seq. The increased sensitivity is particularly evident under low-titre infection conditions, demonstrating the utility of VIPER-seq for the early detection of viral infections and its potential to strengthen plant disease diagnostics, seed health testing, and biosecurity surveillance programs.

items.title: Dual Role of Cx43 in Enhancing CDK4/6 Inhibitor Response and Promoting the Elimination of Therapy-Induced Senescent Tumor Cells
items.abstract_or_text: Breast cancer has become the most prevalent malignancy worldwide. A key clinical advance has been the introduction of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i), that in combination with endocrine therapy has been a major advance for the treatment of luminal (ER⁺/HER2⁻) breast cancer. CDK4/6i induce cell cycle arrest in G1 and cellular senescence improving clinical outputs. However, limited efficacy and therapeutic resistance remain major challenges due to incomplete effects or the failure to eliminate the accumulated tumor senescent cells. Here, we identify connexin 43 (Cx43), a membrane channel protein involved in cell-to-cell communication, identified as a novel target in luminal breast cancer that potentiates the effects of CDK4/6 inhibitors. We found that Cx43 not only reduces tumor cell proliferation by enhancing senescence but also reshapes the Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP) profile. We also demonstrate that, in combination with CDK4/6i, Cx43 reinforces G1 arrest via transcriptional downregulation of E2F targets including CDK4 and CDK6, and through interaction with p21/p27, deepens the senescent state. Importantly, the Cx43-associated senescent phenotype sensitizes tumor cells accumulated under CDK4/6i treatment to the senolytic agent Navitoclax. Our results demonstrate that upregulation of Cx43 in breast cancer reduces proliferation and enhances the clearance of therapy-induced senescent cells. The triple-drug strategy comprising CDK4/6i, Cx43 delivery, and a senolytic drug such as Navitoclax holds great promise for overcoming CDK4/6i resistance and improving clinical outcomes in ER⁺/HER2⁻ breast cancer and may also be applicable to other cancer types that respond to CDK4/6i or other pro-senescence antitumoral drugs.

items.title: Multi-resolution humanness scoring of antibodies via a region-isolated language model
items.abstract_or_text: Antibodies recognized as foreign can elicit anti-drug antibodies that compromise efficacy and safety, making humanness scoring, estimating how human-like a sequence appears, an early, repeated step in antibody development. Widely used scores reduce a variable domain to a single framework-dominated number, leaving the complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) grafted during humanization, diversified by generative models weakly supervised and rarely audited. Here we introduce IgScope, a 23-million-parameter antibody language model trained from scratch that scores humanness at chain, IMGT-region, and residue resolution; a region-isolated attention module confines attention to within-region pairs, and chimeric-sequence training supplies region-level supervision. On 2.38 million held-out chains, masking all framework tokens leaves CDR accuracy unchanged, and back-mutated murine residues in human frameworks are detected at 93.4% accuracy. At chain level, IgScope matches the strongest published correlation with clinical anti-drug-antibody incidence (r = 0.567, n = 217) and outperforms a same-protocol recomputation. Region-level scoring exposes what chain-level scoring conceals: antibodies designed de novo by four generative models pass whole-chain humanness (0.966-0.988), while their CDRs score far below natural (P < 1e-30) in every chain class. Quality control turns the same resolution to the mirror-image question: in humanized-mouse platforms, whose domains are human by design, IgScope scores the domain as human and, in HUGO-Nano chimeric VHHs, isolates only the FR2 signal of four camelid hallmark residues deliberately retained to stabilize the VHH. IgScope gives antibody humanization a verified foundation and generative design an audit.
